a: Name of the database. Must be a valid name containing only letters, numbers, dashes, and underscores.
URL of the RavenDB server. Must include the scheme (http or https), hostname, and port.
Path to a trusted CA certificate file to verify the RavenDB server's certificate.
Path to a client certificate (PEM format) for secured communication.
Type-specific properties dictionary (see examples). Secrets may be inline or loaded from using Ansible lookups.
Desired state of the connection string. If present, the item is created when absent (no in-place updates; existing items are left unchanged). If absent, the item is removed when present.
Name of the database. Must be a valid name containing only letters, numbers, dashes, and underscores.
URL of the RavenDB server. Must include the scheme (http or https), hostname, and port.
Path to a trusted CA certificate file to verify the RavenDB server's certificate.
Path to a client certificate (PEM format) for secured communication.
Dictionary of database-level settings to apply. Keys and values are normalized to strings and compared against current customized settings.
Create the database as encrypted. When true, the module ensures a secret key is assigned (generated or read from file) and distributed to all cluster nodes before creation.
Path to a file that contains the raw encryption key (plain text). Mutually exclusive with generate_encryption_key. Used only when encrypted.
When generate_encryption_key, write the generated key to this local file with safe permissions. Ignored if generate_encryption_key.
If true, asks the server to generate a new encryption key via the admin API. Mutually exclusive with encryption_key. Used only when encrypted.
Number of server nodes to replicate the database to. Must be a positive integer. Only used when creating a database. Required on creation; ignored for existing databases.
Desired state of the database. If present, the database will be created if it does not exist, and settings will be reconciled. If absent, the database will be deleted if it exists.
Optional list of cluster node tags to host this database (fixed placement). When provided, its length must equal replication_factor. Honored only on creation.
Base URL of the RavenDB node to check, e.g. http://node-a:8080 or https://node-a:443.
Path to a CA bundle used to validate the server certificate.
Path to a client certificate for secured clusters.
List of health checks to run.
Interval in seconds between attempts for db_groups_available and db_groups_available_excluding_target.
Max time window in seconds for each selected check before timing out.
Behavior when db_groups_available times out. fail fails the task; continue returns success with timeout noted in results.
Interval in seconds between attempts for node_alive and cluster_connectivity.
Verify the server TLS certificate when using HTTPS. Automatically disabled for IP hosts when running node_alive or cluster_connectivity.
ravendb.ravendb.healthcheck.d: Perform RavenDB node and cluster health checks

a: Name of the database. Must be a valid name containing only letters, numbers, dashes, and underscores.
Name of the index to create, delete, or modify. Must consist only of letters, numbers, dashes, and underscores.
URL of the RavenDB server. Must include the scheme (http or https), hostname, and port.
Path to a trusted CA certificate file to verify the RavenDB server's certificate.
Path to a client certificate (PEM format) for secured communication.
Whether to apply enable/disable operations cluster-wide.
Per-index configuration key/value pairs to reconcile. Keys and values are normalized to strings and compared against the current index definition's configuration.
Dictionary defining the index (map list and optional reduce string). Required when creating a new index. When present for an existing index, differences are applied idempotently.
Operational mode to apply to an existing index (one of enable/disable/pause/resume/reset). If the index does not exist and only mode is provided, the task fails with guidance to create it first.
Desired state of the index. If present, the index will be created if it does not exist, and the definition/configuration will be reconciled. If absent, the index will be deleted if it exists.
The HTTP/HTTPS URL of the cluster leader the module will contact to add the node.
The unique tag for the node (uppercase alphanumeric, 1–4 chars).
The HTTP/HTTPS URL of the node being added.
Path to a CA certificate bundle to verify the server certificate.
Path to a client certificate in PEM format (combined certificate and key). Required for secured clusters (HTTPS with client authentication).
Node type. Use Watcher to add the node as a watcher instead of a full member.
